package.welcome_message: Land in Amman, then 3 exploring days through Dead Sea, then Wadi Rum (2 days).

trip.title: Dead Sea · Wadi Rum
trip.summary: Arrival, then Dead Sea, then Wadi Rum (2 days). Walk outdoors in the morning. Keep the afternoon for shade, meals, or indoor visits.

planning.strategy: You land at 18:15, so arrival night stays in Amman — hotel, a meal, rest. The touring days start the next morning. I put Wadi Rum on the calendar first, then kept the rest of the days on Dead Sea, then Wadi Rum (2 days). It's a hot month, so the outdoor sites go before midday.

hotels.address: Jordan Valley Highway (Dead Sea Road), Sweimeh, Jordan

facts.subcategory: Family Resort with Waterslide and Spa Clinic
facts.notes: 198 rooms, all with private balconies. Four outdoor pools plus a waterslide. The private beach is about 400 metres long and roughly 50 metres from the property, served by a shuttle, with complimentary mud scrub provided. The star rating is contested: the hotel's own marketing claims five stars while aggregators classify it as four, so it is left unset. Check-in is given as 16:00 by one source and 15:00 by another.

202 rooms, each with a private balcony or patio. Pool count is given as four outdoor pools by one source and three interconnected pools by another. Spa treatments require advance reservation. Children under eighteen may stay free with parents. Marked disabled parking with barrier-free access. No verified nightly rate was found during this search.

hotels.name: Ramada Resort by Wyndham Dead Sea

facts.notes: 161 rooms and suites over four floors. The private beach is reached by a complimentary shuttle rather than being directly attached to the property. The northernmost hotel on the Jordanian Dead Sea strip and the closest to the baptism site. Airport shuttle is available at a surcharge.

hotels.name: Kempinski Hotel Ishtar Dead Sea
hotels.address: Dead Sea Road, 18186 Sweimeh, Balqa, Jordan

facts.notes: 345 rooms and suites. Nine outdoor freshwater pools plus a heated indoor pool and a children's pool. The Ishtar Spa has twenty treatment rooms. Seven event venues, the largest for six hundred guests. Standard day passes are not sold; day access is tied to spa bookings and subject to occupancy.

meta.planning_lock:
PLANNING LOCK (hard — plan OVER clusters, then write JSON):
- Fill ALL 3 days (nights=2). No empty/partial days.
- Mandatory destinations (preferredRegions + mustVisit): Dead Sea, Wadi Rum. Plan ONLY in these areas — any other cluster is reference material, not a day.
- Destination→cluster map: Dead Sea→cluster 1 (Karak Governorate · culture, nature, history); Wadi Rum→cluster 0 (Ma'an Governorate · nature, culture, history)
- Day→cluster route (one day per cluster, in this order): D1:C0/Wadi Rum part 1 → D2:C1/Dead Sea → D3:C2/Wadi Rum part 2
- mustVisit entity lock: Wadi Rum→lead with Red Sand Dunes of Wadi Rum (cluster 0)
- Each day draws its POIs, meals and hotel from ITS OWN cluster.
- No entity twice in the whole trip: a POI or restaurant used on one day cannot reappear on another, and lunch and dinner are different places. Two days in the same city are two different clusters — use each cluster's own entities.
- Each day: 3 sights + lunch + dinner (5 entries, 6 max). Two sights only when the cluster has no third worth visiting, and say so. No gap over 90 minutes, no site under 45 minutes, at least 4 hours of sightseeing per full day.
- activity_alternatives come from that cluster's UNUSED entities: never an entity scheduled elsewhere in the trip, and never two scheduled stops as each other's swap.
- One visit, one fee (POIs within 600 m are parts of one site): (no such groups here)
- Lodging requested: rating=4 star, type=hotel. Per-night base (night N = where day N ends): N1(C0): no hotel card — state lodging is not covered; N2(C1): Grand East Hotel Resort & Spa Dead Sea [4-star]
- Money: 899 JOD covers 2 traveller(s) for 3 days (≈299.667 JOD/day for the whole party). Lodging = nightly rate x 2 night(s) x ~1 room(s), arithmetic shown in the notes. aiPriority=comfort → spend the headroom on better-rated entities instead of leaving it idle. SME=(none).
- Entry fees are the last thing to cut: never skip a named destination's main ticketed site to save money, and state what is left of the budget.
- Names/hours/fees: EntityCards only. If a card does not carry a fact (rating, booking requirement, closing day), do not state it.
- Prices: use the card value as-is, multiplied by the party size, and show the arithmetic in the tip ("10 JOD x 4"). If a card has no price, estimate from pricing_level and label it "~N JOD (estimated)".
- Events are reference only: never schedule them in the itinerary or budget.
